questions.subject: HUMAN_GEOGRAPHY
questions.topic: The two direct effects of a depreciation
questions.learningObjective: Identify the two direct effects of a currency depreciation
questions.stem: In my observing log, a currency depreciates; which two effects follow directly?

options.text: Exports cost less abroad and imports cost more at home
Exports cost more abroad and imports cost less at home
Exports rise in price and imports fall in price abroad

options.text: No change in relative prices occurs in trade

questions.explanation: Depreciation lowers export prices in foreign currency and raises import prices in domestic currency. The tempting idea that nothing changes ignores relative price shifts.

questions.subject: HUMAN_GEOGRAPHY
questions.topic: Floating against a fixed exchange rate
questions.learningObjective: Contrast floating and fixed exchange-rate regimes
questions.stem: In my log, compare a floating rate with a fixed rate for a small open economy.

answer.exemplar: A floating rate adjusts automatically to shocks and preserves monetary policy independence, while a fixed rate anchors expectations but sacrifices policy autonomy and requires reserves.

questions.explanation: Floating rates absorb shocks through price adjustment while fixed rates need reserves and policy discipline. The tempting view that fixed rates are costless ignores reserve and autonomy losses.
questions.hint: Weigh automatic adjustment against policy autonomy.

questions.hint: Divide reserves by the monthly outflow.
